newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil subdued as market assesses IPE play.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil subdued as market assesses IPE play.

text.p: NWE gas oil traders kept the brakes firmly applied to physical trade on Wednesday to try to shield themselves against potential price swings caused by a record high physical delivery against the November IPE contract.

The 865,100 tonnes delivered into the contract in the second half of November split traders into bulls and bears, with differences centred on the viability of a play by the dominant long which is believed to be due to take most of the delivery.
"There is a very big divergence of opinion, which is mostly why the market is not going haywire one way or the other," one trader said.
Outright prices rose with Dec IPE futures, which finished $5.50 stronger at $216.50 a tonne on the back of colder weather in the Great Lakes region of the United States and Europe.

But premiums were steady to slightly firmer in thin volumes on both cargo and barge markets. A barge of refinery grade heating oil for late November delivery ex-Antwerp traded at Dec +$8.50, around unchanged.
A barge of low sulphur diesel (-7/-20) traded at Dec +$16.50 ex-Antwerp for late November delivery, slightly firmer.
Low sulphur cargoes were around Dec IPE +$16/18.
